title: Scout S1: kgpt projects data model, project tools and routes — where a repo binding and per-file provenance would live
spec: Read-only scout over /Users/k3ntaw/code/kgpt. Read kernel/kgpt_kernel/projects.py, folders.py, workingset.py, tools/builtin.py (project/working-set/file tools around line 900), gateway/kgpt_gateway/routes/projects.py, kernel/migrations/versions/0016_projects.py, 0017_project_folders.py, 0018_github_connections.py, and documents/store.py for how an attachment records filename, folder, project_id, content hash and how a newer version supersedes an older one (ADR 0014 staleness). Report: (1) tables and columns for projects, folders, working_set, attachments; (2) every project-related tool name with tier and what it returns; (3) every /projects and /folders route; (4) where per-project repo binding (installation_id, owner, repo, base branch, base sha) and per-attachment repo provenance (repo path, blob sha) fit with least churn, naming the migration number to use next (latest is 0025) and the row-level-security pattern new tables must follow (ADR 0014 OWNED_AFTER_0012 note); (5) how "changed since import" can be computed from what is stored. Cite path:line for every claim, one confidence per finding. Do not read web client or modules/github (other scouts).
acceptance: Result lists tables/columns, tools with tiers, and routes with path:line citations
Result names the next migration number and the RLS pattern a new table must follow, with the file that proves it
Result proposes where repo binding and per-file provenance go, with an estimate of files touched

findings.claim: kernel.projects table: id uuid PK default gen_random_uuid(); name text NOT NULL; instructions text; archived boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false; created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(); user_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_USER_DEFAULT REFERENCES kernel.users(id).

kernel.project_folders table: id uuid PK; project_id uuid NOT NULL FK kernel.projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; parent_id uuid FK kernel.project_folders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, nullable (NULL = project root); name text NOT NULL; created_at timestamptz; user_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT. Unique index on (project_id, parent_id, lower(name)) NULLS NOT DISTINCT.

kernel.working_set table: conversation_id uuid NOT NULL FK kernel.conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; attachment_id uuid NOT NULL FK kernel.attachments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; added_at timestamptz DEFAULT now(); user_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT; PRIMARY KEY (conversation_id, attachment_id).

kernel.attachments table accumulates columns across migrations: id uuid PK, conversation_id uuid FK conversations ON DELETE CASCADE nullable, filename text NOT NULL, media_type text NOT NULL, size_bytes bigint NOT NULL, sha256 text NOT NULL, direction text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'upload' (check upload|generated), created_at timestamptz (0007); attribution text nullable (0008); project_id uuid FK kernel.projects(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, nullable (0016); folder_id uuid FK kernel.project_folders(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, nullable (0017). attachments is also in the frozen OWNED_TABLES list, so it carries a user_id ownership column from the 0010-0012 ownership migrations.

kernel.github_connections table: id uuid PK; installation_id bigint NOT NULL (GitHub's own id); account text NOT NULL (display name); connected_at timestamptz DEFAULT now(); user_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT. Unique index on (user_id, installation_id) — one row per person per installation, not per project.

Nine project-related tools exist, all defined via registry.tool in tools/builtin.py: list_projects (READ, projects.py:900) returns {projects, none_yet}; create_project (WRITE_LOCAL, 929) returns {project, created}; set_project_instructions (WRITE_LOCAL, 964) returns {project, cost_is_per_turn}; list_project_files (READ, 996) returns {files, none_yet}; put_file_in_play (WRITE_LOCAL, 1022) returns {in_play}; take_file_out_of_play (WRITE_LOCAL, 1051) returns {removed, was_not_in_play}; refresh_working_set (WRITE_LOCAL, 1076) returns {moved_to_newer_version, nothing_was_stale}; put_conversation_in_project (WRITE_LOCAL, 1099) returns {in_project, taken_out, files_did_not_move}; put_file_in_project (WRITE_LOCAL, 1143) returns {filed, filename, attachment_id, in_project}.

17 project/folder routes in gateway/kgpt_gateway/routes/projects.py: GET /projects:73, POST /projects:78, GET /projects/{project_id}:87, PATCH /projects/{project_id}/name:95, PUT /projects/{project_id}/instructions:105, PATCH /projects/{project_id}/archived:120, GET /projects/{project_id}/files:130, PUT /files/{attachment_id}/project:139, PUT /conversations/{conversation_id}/project:150, GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/working-set:167, GET /projects/{project_id}/tree:205, POST /projects/{project_id}/folders:217, PATCH /folders/{folder_id}/name:228, DELETE /folders/{folder_id}:238, PUT /files/{attachment_id}/folder:254, GET /projects/{project_id}/zip:265, GET /folders/{folder_id}/zip:273.
The latest applied migration is 0025_live_activity_tokens.py, so the next migration number to use is 0026.

open_questions: Is a project-repo binding meant to be 1:1 (one repo per project) or should a project support multiple repo bindings? This changes whether columns-on-projects or a join table is the right least-churn call.

Should attachment repo provenance be recorded only for files imported from a repo (import flow, not yet seen — likely in modules/github, excluded from this scout), or retrofitted onto the generic upload path in documents/store.py:save()?
suggested_next: Have the scout covering modules/github report the shape of any existing GitHub file-fetch/import code path, since that is where repo_path/blob_sha would need to be threaded into store.save() calls.

Confirm whether the Planner wants a single 0026 migration covering both the project-binding columns and the attachment-provenance columns, or two atomic migrations (0026, 0027) per the orchestrator's ATOMIC-spec convention.
